headline_original: Iran accuses the US of targeting a tanker near Kharg Island, and other Mideast news
headline_cs: Írán obvinil USA z útoku na tanker u Kharg Island
summary_cs: Íránská státní televize uvedla, že americké střely zasáhly íránský tanker poblíž Kharg Island v Perském zálivu. USA se bezprostředně nevyjádřily; pokud se útok potvrdí, jde o další konkrétní eskalaci poblíž klíčového íránského ropného exportního uzlu a zvyšuje riziko odvety i dalšího omezení regionální přepravy ropy.

market_context_at_prediction.notes: The new information is a claimed U.S. strike on an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island. The dominant incremental mechanism is higher oil-supply and retaliation risk. Firm DXY and high U.S. yields limit gold upside, while already-elevated oil increases the sensitivity of European and Japanese equity indices to further escalation.

learning_prior.reason: No verified relevant ACTIONABLE context-aware segment was identified that justified changing the forecast confidence. EARLY_SIGNAL evidence was treated as advisory only and INSUFFICIENT evidence caused no adjustment.

predictions.mechanism: A fresh military escalation near a critical Iranian oil-export area raises safe-haven demand and geopolitical risk premia, although firm U.S. yields and DXY cap the upside.
predictions.invalidation: The strike is credibly denied or rapidly de-escalated, no retaliation follows, and oil/risk premia fall materially before markets reopen.

predictions.mechanism: Germany is highly exposed to imported energy costs; a higher Middle East oil-risk premium raises inflation and margin pressure while reducing risk appetite.
predictions.invalidation: Rapid de-escalation, a clear denial of the strike, or a material drop in crude prices before the European open.

predictions.mechanism: Higher oil and geopolitical risk premia are a headwind for European growth-sensitive equities and can tighten financial conditions through inflation expectations.
predictions.invalidation: No follow-through in oil or regional tensions and a broad global risk-on move into the next European session.

predictions.mechanism: A renewed energy shock and geopolitical escalation raise input costs and risk aversion across European cyclicals, though energy exposure can offset part of the pressure.
predictions.invalidation: Oil gives back the risk premium or the reported strike is not confirmed and geopolitical tensions ease.

predictions.mechanism: Japan is a major energy importer, so higher oil-risk premia combine with existing yen strength to pressure exporter margins and domestic purchasing power.
predictions.invalidation: Crude prices fall sharply, geopolitical tensions de-escalate, or a strong global risk-on move overwhelms the energy and currency headwinds.

predictions.mechanism: Escalation raises the equity risk premium and oil-driven inflation risk, while already-high Treasury yields leave less valuation cushion for broad U.S. equities.
predictions.invalidation: The geopolitical report is denied or contained and oil prices retreat materially before U.S. markets reopen.

predictions.mechanism: Higher geopolitical and inflation risk can keep Treasury yields elevated and raise discount rates, a particular valuation headwind for long-duration technology shares.
predictions.invalidation: Treasury yields and oil fall while the conflict de-escalates, allowing risk appetite to recover before the next U.S. session.
